We present TACT, a dataset for modeling the integration of task-oriented and chitchat dialogues with natural mode transitions and recoverable structures. TACT enables training models that can manage complex dialogue flows, including multi-turn mode shifts and returns to prior tasks.
outputs: Generated agent responses in multi-turn dialogues, including task-oriented replies and chitchat turns.
The outputs are conversational responses in multi-turn dialogues that alternate between task-oriented and chitchat modes, with an emphasis on smooth transitions and recovery to prior tasks.

We use three metrics to assess a model's task-handling abilities. (1) Mode Selection Accuracy and F1... (2) Intent Detection Accuracy... (3) Mode+Intent Joint Accuracy...

The LLM judge (GEMINI-2.5-PRO) assessed sensibleness, specificity, interestingness, and transition naturalness ... We also conducted pairwise comparisons between the target model and GPT-4O ... using GPT-4O‑MINI as a judging model.

The judging model, GPT-4O-MINI scores each dialogue on three criteria: (1) Intent Accuracy, which checks whether the user intent is correctly conveyed and executed; (2) Transition Quality, which assesses whether mode switches are contextually justified; and (3) Dialogue Naturalness, which evaluates fluency and coherence.

Evaluators were given evaluation instructions and asked to rate responses on sensibleness, specificity, interestingness, transition naturalness, and overall quality.

Annotators were provided with a short guideline and a dedicated web interface. The instruction included evaluation criteria such as whether the response makes sense, is specific, is interesting, and whether the transition is natural.
